llm.summary: The skill's described purpose (local sanitization + cloud detection) is plausible, but there are several inconsistencies and missing provenance/credential details that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a legitimate security plugin (local gateway + cloud detection) and the runtime actions it will perform. However, the registry metadata lists no source/homepage while the docs repeatedly point to a GitHub repo and an npm package (@openguardrails/moltguard). That mismatch (registry claims 'unknown' source/homepage) reduces provenance confidence. The skill also claims 'all sensitive data is sanitized locally' but simultaneously requires activation/registration with a cloud service for detection and billing — this is plausible but the boundary claims are high-impact and should be verified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to installing the plugin via the openclaw CLI, restarting the gateway, testing a bundled sample file, and using commands (/og_status, /og_sanitize, /og_config). The doc asks the agent/user to inspect code on GitHub and local install paths. It does not instruct the agent to read arbitrary user files beyond the sample and documented credential/config paths. Still, the SKILL.md gives the agent discretion to announce and block tool calls based on cloud responses — that is expected for a security plugin but expands what the agent may disclose to the user and what metadata is sent upstream.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This registry entry contains no install spec, but the SKILL.md instructs running 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard', which will fetch a published npm package. Installing code from npm is a non-trivial operation (archive extraction and execution) and should be treated as higher risk than instruction-only skills. The doc suggests ways to verify npm ↔ GitHub provenance, but the registry's missing source/homepage and the random owner ID mean the installer should verify the package tarball exactly matches the GitHub source before trusting it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, yet the documentation describes activation, per-agent API keys, billing, and stored credentials (e.g., credentials.json under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/). That implies the runtime will accept and store an OpenGuardrails API key and possibly email/agent ID — sensitive data not declared up-front in the registry. The lack of a declared 'primary credential' in metadata is a transparency gap; users should explicitly expect to provide a cloud API key and understand what is stored and transmitted (even if 'sanitized').
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced always-on) and normal autonomous invocation are used. The skill will register/activate and persist credentials/config under the user's OpenClaw directories, which is typical for plugins. This persistence plus cloud connectivity increases blast radius if the installed package is malicious or has supply-chain compromise — so treat persistence as expected but verify installed code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill looks like a real security plugin but has provenance and transparency gaps. Before installing: 1) Do NOT install into a production or highly privileged environment — test in an isolated VM or sandbox. 2) Verify the npm package matches the GitHub source (npm pack, tarball diff against repo) as the SKILL.md suggests. 3) Inspect the actual package contents (especially agent/sanitizer.ts, index.ts, platform-client/) for any unexpected endpoints or code that sends uninterpreted data off-host. 4) Expect to provide an OpenGuardrails API key to activate billing/quotas; confirm what is stored locally and what sanitized metadata is sent (use tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch to validate). 5) If you cannot verify provenance or you refuse any cloud transmission of metadata, do not install. 6) After installation, monitor ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/ and network traffic and be ready to revoke/delete credentials if anything looks off.
